India's Reform Express: A deregulation drive for growth

Over the last two years, the Centre and States have undertaken efforts to simplify, rationalise and modernise India's regulatory landscape to improve Ease of Doing Business.

100+*reforms by the Government of India
1,000+*reforms across States and UTs

* These reforms are a compilation from public sources and may not be exhaustive.

Highlights
133 quality control orders and technical regulations revoked or suspended

Central reforms

Tap a sector, then a reform, to see what changed and the official document.

Environment
Mandatory 33% green cover requirement rationalisedMoEFCC · 29 Oct 2025

Before

A blanket 33 to 40% of plot area had to be kept as green cover by every industrial unit, irrespective of category. An estimated 1.2 lakh hectares of industrial land stayed locked as a result.

Now

Green cover set at 10% for new industrial estates, 15% for Red category units and 10% for Orange category units, and made optional for Green and White category units.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Continuity of SEIAA and SEACMoEFCC · 5 Mar 2026

Before

SEIAA and SEAC were reconstituted by the Central Government every 3 years, and reconstitution often took 6 to 9 months. Clearances stopped entirely in the interim.

Now

An interim committee keeps environmental clearances moving when the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) or State Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC) is not in place.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Consent to Operate made perpetualMoEFCC · 23 Jan 2026

Before

Consent to Operate needed renewal every 5, 10 or 15 years depending on category. Each renewal needed a physical inspection that only State boards could carry out.

Now

Consent to Operate from the pollution control board is perpetual, and registered third-party environmental auditors may carry out inspections.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Central siting distance norms removedMoEFCC · 23 Jan 2026

Before

Blanket distance-based siting norms set by the Centre restricted where projects could be located and took no account of local conditions.

Now

Central siting norms are removed, for example the 500 metre waterbody buffer for Red category industries.

View document (opens in a new tab)
No separate clearance for units inside covered estatesMoEFCC · 25 Nov 2025

Before

Units inside parks with a park-level Environmental Clearance also needed their own clearance, even for activities on the park's approved list.

Now

No unit-level Environmental Clearance is needed where the industrial estate's existing clearance already covers the activity.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Published baseline data replaces fresh collectionMoEFCC · 6 Apr 2026

Before

Primary baseline data collection takes 3 to 4 months and was repeated even where data for the area already existed.

Now

Baseline environmental data is published on the government portal and used where it already exists for the area.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Third-party inspection and auto-renewal of consents in GoaGoa SPCB · 11 Jul 2025

Before

Only the State Pollution Control Board could inspect units for consent renewals.

Now

Accredited third-party agencies inspect units for renewal of Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate, and renewals are automatic.

View document (opens in a new tab)
More industries moved to the White CategoryMoEFCC · 8 Jul 2026

Before

These industries needed both Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate before the revision.

Now

Industries added to the White Category list are exempt from Consent to Establish and Consent to Operate.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Self-certified Consent to Establish for micro and small unitsMoEFCC · 23 Jan 2026

Before

Micro and small units inside notified industrial estates had to obtain Consent to Establish separately.

Now

Consent to Establish is self-certified for micro and small units in notified industrial areas.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Restaurants with up to 100 seats moved to WhiteCPCB · 20 Jul 2026

Before

Small, low-polluting eateries fell under the consent regime, with compliance costs out of proportion to their pollution.

Now

Restaurants, dhabas and eateries with up to 100 seats are classified under the White Category.

View document (opens in a new tab)
CPCB categorisation for hotels relaxedCPCB · 20 Jul 2026

Before

Hotels were classified only as Red, Orange or Green. Very small hotels had no lower category, and classification ignored the fuel and systems they used.

Now

Hotels, motels and resorts with 101 to 300 rooms are placed under Orange, and those with up to 20 rooms under White where they use clean or gaseous kitchen fuel and manage wastewater properly.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Companies Act
CSR applies from ₹10 crore net profitMCA · 2026

Before

CSR applied at net worth of ₹500 crore, turnover of ₹1,000 crore or net profit of ₹5 crore. An estimated 4,000 mid-sized companies came under mandatory CSR as a result.

Now

The net profit threshold for CSR applicability is raised to ₹10 crore.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Immediate strike-off for dormant companiesMCA · 2026

Before

A company had to stay inactive for two financial years before applying for strike-off. The estimated compliance cost was about ₹200 crore nationally.

Now

Companies with no operations and no liabilities can apply for strike-off immediately.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Fast-track mergers need 75% consentMCA · 2026

Before

Fast-track mergers needed approval from 90% of shareholders and 90% of creditors by value. Approvals took 9 to 12 months.

Now

The approval threshold for fast-track mergers is reduced to 75% consent.

View document (opens in a new tab)
CSR Committee needed from ₹1 croreMCA · 2026

Before

Companies with CSR obligations of ₹50 lakh or more had to form a CSR Committee.

Now

The CSR obligation that triggers a CSR Committee is raised to ₹1 crore.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Three months to transfer unspent CSR fundsMCA · 2026

Before

Companies had 30 days after year-end to move unspent funds into an Unspent CSR Account.

Now

Unspent CSR funds for ongoing projects can be transferred up to 3 months after year-end.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Three-year projections dropped from Section 8 applicationsMCA · 8 Apr 2026

Before

Applicants had to estimate annual income and expenditure for the next three years.

Now

Speculative three-year income and expenditure estimates are deleted from Section 8 licence applications.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Company names checked against trademarks in real timeMCA · 8 Apr 2026

Before

Company-name approval and trademark clearance ran as two separate searches, at the MCA registry and at the Trade Marks Registry.

Now

The MCA and Trade Marks databases are integrated for real-time company-name validation.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Small company limits raised to ₹10 crore and ₹100 croreMCA · 1 Dec 2025

Before

Companies crossed the small company threshold at ₹4 crore paid-up capital or ₹40 crore turnover, which pulled mid-sized firms into the full compliance regime.

Now

The paid-up capital limit for a small company is raised to ₹10 crore and the turnover limit to ₹100 crore.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Trade
FDI allowed in inventory-based e-commerce for exportsDPIIT · 23 Jul 2026

Before

Holding inventory for MSME exporters risked reclassifying a platform as inventory-based, a model ineligible for FDI, so platforms avoided supporting MSME exports.

Now

FDI is allowed on the inventory-based e-commerce model for exports of goods manufactured in India.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Value cap removed for courier exportsDGFT and CBIC · 27 to 31 Mar 2026

Before

Courier exports were capped at ₹10 lakh per consignment under Para 9.05 of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023.

Now

The ₹10 lakh per-consignment value cap for courier exports is removed.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Five-year tax exemption for suppliers to electronics contract manufacturersMoF · 2026

Before

Storing inventory or capital equipment in India could create a Permanent Establishment and expose a foreign firm's global income to Indian tax.

Now

Foreign companies supplying goods to electronics contract manufacturers are exempt from tax for 5 years, until tax year 2030 to 31.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Self-sealing permission made perpetualMoF · 27 Mar 2026

Before

Permission to seal export containers at the exporter's own premises was time-bound and needed periodic renewal.

Now

Self-sealing (factory stuffing) permission is perpetual for manufacturing and merchant exporters.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Advance Pricing Agreements processed fasterCBDT · 20 Mar 2026

Before

Slow processing of Advance Pricing Agreements left multinational companies uncertain about tax on cross-border transfer pricing.

Now

The Advance Pricing Agreement programme is restructured to match global processing standards.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Permanent Establishment exposure clarifiedMoF · 2026

Before

Foreign companies supplying capital goods and tooling to Indian electronics contract manufacturers did not know whether this created a taxable presence in India.

Now

Permanent Establishment exposure for foreign suppliers of capital goods and tooling is clarified under the Income Tax Act.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Safe harbour for components in bonded warehousesMoF · 2026

Before

If component vendors transferred title to the brand owner before delivery to contract manufacturers, the brand owner's aggregator role became taxable in India.

Now

Non-residents warehousing components in bonded facilities get a safe harbour, with profit taken as 2% of invoice value and taxed at 0.7%.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Petroleum and explosives
District Magistrate NOC replaced by self-declarationDPIIT · 5 Jun 2026

Before

PESO licences needed a prior NOC from the District Magistrate, adding several months.

Now

The District Magistrate NOC for PESO licences is replaced with self-declaration.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Simpler approvals for ISO tanks and containersDPIIT · 5 Jun 2026

Before

Each domestic movement of an ISO tank or container needed separate approval. Filled containers could not be used for static storage and were certified only for the named gas or product.

Now

ISO tank and container approvals are simplified and wider use is permitted.

View document (opens in a new tab)
LNG in cryogenic cylinders at LS-1 premisesPESO · 25 Mar 2026

Before

LNG could not be filled or stored in cryogenic cylinders within LS-1 premises.

Now

LNG filling and storage in cryogenic cylinders is permitted in LS-1 licensed premises. Wider fuel access is estimated at 0.2 to 0.4 billion people.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Risk-based storage normsDPIIT · 5 Jun 2026

Before

Rules fixed setback distances, sump capacity, cylinder stacking, vessels per group and mechanised handling, irrespective of risk.

Now

Storage norms are rationalised on a risk-based approach.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Shared warehouse storage allowedDPIIT · 5 Feb 2026

Before

Leasing storage was not permitted, and one facility could not store solvents and gases for several industries.

Now

Shared warehouse storage is allowed, including leased facilities run by third-party logistics providers.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Night loading approved once at licensingDPIIT · 2 Apr 2026

Before

Each site needed a separate approval from the Chief Controller to load or unload petroleum and compressed gases between sunset and sunrise.

Now

Night-hour loading and unloading is approved once, at the initial licensing stage.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Mobile refuelling units allowedDPIIT · 10 Jun 2026

Before

All gas filling and dispensing had to happen within licensed premises. Mobile CNG dispensing was refused unless the site itself was declared, inspected and licensed.

Now

Mobile refuelling units are allowed to operate.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Pharmaceuticals
Intimation for test quantities of new drugsMoHFW · 20 Jan 2026

Before

Prior permission was needed even for small test quantities.

Now

An intimation pathway replaces prior permission to manufacture new drugs and investigational new drugs for examination, test or analysis.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Test licence decisions in 45 working daysMoHFW · 20 Jan 2026

Before

Regulatory decisions could take up to 90 working days.

Now

The approval timeline for test licence applications is halved from 90 to 45 working days.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Parallel review of clinical trial applicationsCDSCO · 11 May 2026

Before

Applicants usually approached Ethics Committees only after CDSCO clearance, so the two reviews ran one after the other.

Now

CDSCO and Ethics Committees process clinical trial applications in parallel.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Specialist cadres for drug approvalsMoF · 2026

Before

CDSCO's workload grew across new drugs, BA/BE studies, medical devices and clinical trials without a matching increase in technical staff, which caused backlogs.

Now

Specialist cadres are created for drug approvals.

View document (opens in a new tab)
MSMEs
Small companies exempted from CSRMCA · 23 Mar 2026

Before

CSR applied once a company crossed net worth, turnover or profit thresholds of ₹500 crore, ₹1,000 crore or ₹5 crore.

Now

Small companies are proposed to be exempted from mandatory CSR.

View document (opens in a new tab)
One board meeting a year for small companiesMCA · 23 Mar 2026

Before

At least two board meetings a year were required.

Now

The board meeting requirement for small companies is proposed to be reduced to one a year.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Relaxed auditor appointment for small companiesMCA · 23 Mar 2026

Before

Small companies were generally required to appoint auditors under the Companies Act.

Now

The auditor appointment requirement is proposed to be relaxed for small companies.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Healthcare
For-profit companies allowed to set up medical colleges and institutionsNMC · 17 Feb 2026

Before

Only societies, trusts and Section 8 not-for-profit companies could set up medical colleges.

Now

All companies registered under the Companies Act, including for-profit companies, can set up medical colleges.

View document (opens in a new tab)
150-seat cap on MBBS intake removedNMC · 23 Apr 2026

Before

No college could admit more than 150 MBBS students a year.

Now

The 150-seat annual intake cap per medical college is removed.

Population ceiling on MBBS seats removedNMC · 23 Apr 2026

Before

States had to stay under 100 MBBS seats per 10 lakh population before new colleges were permitted. All five southern States had crossed this ratio, which blocked new colleges there.

Now

The ceiling of 100 MBBS seats per 10 lakh population is removed.

Essentiality Certificate for medical collegesNMC · 15 Jul 2026

Before

The Essentiality Certificate required the State to re-confirm need, feasibility, land and building clearances, which duplicated checks made elsewhere.

Now

The State Essentiality Certificate for new medical colleges is proposed for removal.

One registration to practise medicine in any StateNMC · 11 Aug 2026

Before

A doctor who moved to another State had to register again with that State's Medical Council and obtain a fresh licence before practising there.

Now

A doctor registered with one State Medical Council receives a Unique Identification Number on the National Medical Register and is proposed to be eligible to practise in any State or Union Territory without fresh registration or licence there. Applications go through one unified portal, and the State and National registers are synchronised automatically.

Food safety
FSSAI registration threshold raised to ₹1.5 croreFSSAI · 13 Mar 2026

Before

Thresholds had not changed since the 2011 Regulations, so food businesses with turnover of about ₹50 lakh fell under State licensing.

Now

The registration threshold is raised from ₹12 lakh to ₹1.5 crore, and the State licence threshold from ₹20 to 30 crore to ₹50 crore.

View document (opens in a new tab)
FSSAI licences made perpetualFSSAI · 10 Mar 2026

Before

Licences ran for 1 to 5 years and needed repeated renewal.

Now

FSSAI licences and registrations are valid in perpetuity.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Risk-based third-party food inspectionsFSSAI · 10 Mar 2026

Before

Inspections did not differ by risk, so low-risk units were over-inspected.

Now

Third-party inspections are randomised and risk-based: annual for high-risk food businesses and once in 3 years for low-risk ones.

View document (opens in a new tab)
One annual date for labelling changesFSSAI · 15 Jan 2025

Before

Ad hoc enforcement dates forced food businesses to discard pre-printed packaging and made planning difficult.

Now

Labelling amendments take effect on a single annual date, 1 July, with one year's lead time.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Legal metrology
Weights and measures licences replaced by registrationDoCA · 2026

Before

Manufacturers, dealers and repairers all needed licences.

Now

Licences for manufacturers, dealers and repairers of weights and measures are replaced with registration.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Approved test centres verify 23 categoriesDoCA · 8 May 2026

Before

Government Approved Test Centres could verify only a short list of instruments, so verification depended on government capacity.

Now

Government Approved Test Centres can verify 23 categories of weights and measures.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Customary units allowed alongside standard unitsDoCA · 18 May 2026

Before

Standard metric units were mandatory even where customary units were used in trade.

Now

Customary units may be declared alongside standard units.

View document (opens in a new tab)
No permission to make non-standard measures for exportDoCA · 12 Mar 2026

Before

Prior Central Government permission was required.

Now

Manufacturing non-standard weights and measures for export no longer needs permission.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Packaged commodity registrations valid until cancelledDoCA · 29 May 2026

Before

Certificates needed periodic renewal.

Now

Registration certificates under the Packaged Commodities Rules are valid until cancelled.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Building code
Building standards confirmed as voluntaryBIS · 30 Apr 2026

Before

The Code's drafting left unclear whether its provisions applied directly or only when adopted under State or local law.

Now

The voluntary nature of the national building standards is clarified.

View on BIS website (opens in a new tab)
Performance-based fire safety designBIS · 30 Apr 2026

Before

Fire-safety provisions were largely prescriptive.

Now

A performance-based design framework is introduced for fire and life safety.

View on BIS website (opens in a new tab)
Parts 0, 1 and 2 removed or rationalisedBIS · 30 Apr 2026

Before

Parts 0, 1 and 2 covered integrated planning, definitions and administration, which overlapped with State and urban local body laws.

Now

Parts 0, 1 and 2 are removed or rationalised to end overlap with State and local regulations.

View on BIS website (opens in a new tab)
Development control left to States and local bodiesBIS · 30 Apr 2026

Before

The Code covered development control and general building requirements, though land use, building permission and local planning are mainly State and local subjects.

Now

Development control and general building requirements (Part 3) are left to States, UTs and urban local bodies.

View on BIS website (opens in a new tab)
Non-core provisions removedBIS · 30 Apr 2026

Before

These provisions were operational, or already regulated by MoEFCC and sector-specific laws.

Now

Construction management, site practice, landscaping, signage and asset management provisions are removed.

View on BIS website (opens in a new tab)
Height caps removed for hospitals and industryBIS · 30 Apr 2026

Before

Hospital buildings were capped at 30 metres and industrial buildings at 50 metres, even where site conditions, technology and fire-safety measures allowed taller buildings.

Now

Height restrictions are removed for uses including hospitals, industry and mixed use.

View on BIS website (opens in a new tab)
Quality Control Orders
40 QCOs on plastics and polymers revokedDCPC · 12 Nov 2025

Before

These QCOs raised input costs and constrained sourcing for industries such as textiles and packaging.

Now

40 QCOs on plastics and polymers are revoked, including polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC, ABS, EVA, polycarbonate, polyurethane, ethylene glycol and acetic acid.

View on ministry website (opens in a new tab)
14 QCOs on base metals revokedMinistry of Mines · 13 Nov 2025

Before

These QCOs affected medical devices, automotive and engineering manufacturing.

Now

14 QCOs on base metals are rescinded, covering primary lead, refined zinc, refined nickel, tin ingot, nickel, copper, aluminium and aluminium alloys.

View document (opens in a new tab)
54 steel QCOs suspendedMinistry of Steel · 20 Nov 2025

Before

Steel QCOs constrained raw-material supply for automotive and MSME industries.

Now

54 QCOs are suspended for specified steel categories, and retained for construction, pressure-vessel and pipe categories.

View document (opens in a new tab)
No NOC for non-QCO steel importsMinistry of Steel · 20 Nov 2025

Before

Imports of steel grades not covered by a QCO still needed an NOC, and the Steel Import Monitoring System asked for 56 data fields.

Now

The NOC requirement for non-QCO steel imports is revoked, and Steel Import Monitoring System data fields are cut from 56 to 20.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Machinery safety regulation revokedMinistry of Heavy Industries · 13 Nov 2025

Before

The Omnibus Technical Regulation imposed safety certification requirements on machinery and equipment.

Now

The Omnibus Technical Regulation for machinery and equipment safety is revoked (20 items).

View document (opens in a new tab)
2 QCOs on electronics components revokedDPIIT · 12 Jan 2026

Before

These two inputs for electronics manufacturing needed QCO certification.

Now

QCOs on pressure-sensitive adhesive tapes and flux-cored solder wire are rescinded.

View document (opens in a new tab)
3 QCOs on cross-recessed screws suspendedMinistry of Steel · 20 Jun 2026

Before

Cross-recessed screws needed QCO certification.

Now

QCOs on cross-recessed screws are suspended for three years.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Ports and shipping
Longer clearance validity for port projectsMoEFCC · 20 May 2026

Before

Validity was 10 years, extendable by 1, despite the long gestation and phased development of port projects.

Now

Environmental Clearance validity for ports, harbours, breakwaters and dredging is proposed at 15 years, extendable by up to 5.

View document (opens in a new tab)
Mines
Self-certified minor changes to mining plansIBM · 1 Jun 2026

Before

Every mining-plan change, including minor changes to infrastructure or equipment, needed prior Indian Bureau of Mines approval.

Now

Self-certification covers 15 categories of minor mining-plan changes, with intimation to the Indian Bureau of Mines.

Help build a single source of truth on business approvals

Licences, permits, NOCs, registrations and renewals are spread across many laws and offices. Tell us about the approvals you know, and together we will build one complete list of what it takes to do business in India.

      Had trouble with a regulation? We'd like to hear from you.
